A 49-year-old male presents to the emergency department with sudden, severe abdominal pain that
began while he was watching television at home, prompting an immediate call to emergency services.

His medical history includes obesity, smoking, alcoholism, hypertension, and osteoarthritis. Current
medications are lisinopril and ibuprofen. On examination, his temperature is 98.6°F (36.9°C), blood
pressure is 113/94 mmHg, pulse is 129/min, respirations are 27/min, and oxygen saturation is 97% on
room air. The patient appears to be in an antalgic position on the stretcher. Abdominal examination
reveals rigidity, rebound tenderness, and hypoactive bowel sounds. What is the most appropriate next
step in management? Answer Choices: (A) NPO, IV fluids, and analgesics (B) Colonoscopy (C) Barium
swallow study (D) Exploratory laparotomy (E) Serum lipase and amylase levels (F) Abdominal
radiograph (G) MRI of the abdomen and pelvis (H) CT scan of the abdomen with contrast (I) Abdominal
ultrasound (J) Urgent laparotomy
 A. CT scan of the abdomen with contrast
B. Colonoscopy
C. Urgent laparotomy

E. Abdominal radiograph
